takeaway: Angiotensin II, a potent vasoconstrictor made through the renin–angiotensin system, is released in hypovolaemia.

question.text: Which is a feature of the physiology of angiotensin II?
question.say: Which is a feature of the physiology of angiotensin two?

answer.say: The answer is: released in hypovolaemia.

lines.say: This water tank is almost empty and very thirsty. That is hypovolaemia, a low blood volume.

lines.text: Renin turns angiotensinogen into angiotensin I.
lines.say: Low volume switches on the renin–angiotensin system. Renin converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin one.
Angiotensin one is then converted into angiotensin two, our muscular hero.

lines.text: One of the most potent vasoconstrictors.
lines.say: (laugh) He squeezes the blood vessel hard. Angiotensin two is one of the most potent vasoconstrictors in the body.

lines.text: Squeezing vessels holds up blood pressure.
lines.say: Narrowing the vessels helps hold up blood pressure when the volume is low.

lines.text: Remember: angiotensin II is released in hypovolaemia.
lines.say: Remember: angiotensin two, the great squeezer, is released in hypovolaemia.
